title.narrative: Kenya - Nature Based Solutions for the Future

description.narrative:
The Nature-based Solutions project harnesses the power of nature to tackle the climate crisis today. Bringing together the complimentary expertise humanitarian response and environmental conservation, the Red Cross and WWF employ Nature-based Solutions to increase climate and disaster risk resilience for communities in Lamu, Kenya. Overall, this partnership offers a unique opportunity to leverage the expertise of four members of leading humanitarian and environmental organisations to influence wide-scale change; shifting the thinking of policy makers, private sector, and other donors to invest in NbS for the long term. The overall impact of project is communities in Lamu County are resilient to climate change and disasters. The project outcomes include.
NbS related policies and regulations are in place and integrated into national and county level legal frameworks. Ecosystems are restored and communities access its benefits. Communities have increased adaptive capacity to natural and anthropogenic shocks.
The project aims to impact policy by building the capacity of communities and other stakeholders to influence decisions on environmental protection, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. This will result in an enhanced natural capital, and increased resilience to climate change and other shocks, like flooding and drought. Consequently, there will be reduced devastation due to climatic shocks, less expense on emergency for disasters, increased access to ecosystem services (e.g., clean water, fodder, firewood, non-timber forest products) and greater awareness of the benefits NbS can provide. By creating an interplay between policy and ecosystem restoration, the Lamu community will further benefit from NbS, such as broader livelihood support, enhanced biodiversity, carbon sequestration, and increased opportunities for funding. The project further aims to leverage learnings over the next two years (July 2024 – June 2026) to influence the wider development and environmental sectors, decision makers with a view to inspiring and influencing greater investment in Nature-based Solutions
